'''Nikolai Grigorievich Chebotaryov''' (often spelled '''Chebotarov''' or '''Chebotarev'''; {{langx|ru|Никола́й Григо́рьевич Чеботарёв}}; {{langx|uk|Мико́ла Григо́рович Чеботарьо́в}}; {{Gregorian to Julian|15 June 1894}} – 2 July 1947) was a Soviet [[mathematician]].<ref>{{MacTutor|id=Chebotaryov|title=Nikolai Grigorievich Chebotaryov}}.</ref> He is best known for the [[Chebotaryov density theorem]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://websites.math.leidenuniv.nl/algebra/chebotarev.pdf|first1=H. W.|last1=Lenstra|first2=P.|last2=Stevenhagen|title=Chebotarëv and his density theorem|journal=[[Mathematical Intelligencer]]|volume=18|issue=2|year=1996|pages=26–37|doi=10.1007/BF03027290|s2cid=14089091}}.</ref>

He was a student of [[Dmitry Grave]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=73922|name=Nikolay Grigorievich Chebotarev}}</ref> Chebotaryov worked on the algebra of polynomials, in particular examining the distribution of the zeros. He also studied [[Galois theory]] and wrote a textbook on the subject titled ''Basic Galois Theory''.
His ideas were used by [[Emil Artin]] to prove the [[Artin reciprocity law]].<ref>{{Cite web| title=Artin reciprocity and Mersenne primes | url=https://websites.math.leidenuniv.nl/algebra/artin.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060209010946/http://websites.math.leidenuniv.nl:80/algebra/artin.pdf | archive-date=2006-02-09}}</ref>
He worked with his student Anatoly Dorodnov on a generalization of the [[quadrature of the lune]],<ref>{{citation|title=The problem of squarable lunes|journal=[[American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=107|issue=7|year=2000|pages=645–651|jstor=2589121|first=M. M.|last=Postnikov|authorlink=Mikhail Postnikov|doi=10.2307/2589121}}. Translated from Postnikov's 1963 Russian book on [[Galois theory]]</ref> and proved the conjecture now known as the [[Chebotarev theorem on roots of unity]].

==Early life==
Nikolai Chebotaryov was born on 15 June 1894 in [[Kamianets-Podilskyi]], [[Russian Empire]] (now in [[Ukraine]]). He entered the department of physics and mathematics at [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv|Kiev University]]<!--See WP:KIEV--> in 1912. In 1928, he became a professor at [[Kazan Federal University|Kazan University]], remaining there for the rest of his life. He died on 2 July 1947. He was an atheist.<ref>{{Cite web| title=Naming Infinity: A True Story of Religious Mysticism and Mathematical Creativity | url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201401/rnoti-p62.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203053309/http://www.ams.org/notices/201401/rnoti-p62.pdf | archive-date=2014-02-03}}</ref> On 14 May 2010, a memorial plaque for Nikolai Chebotaryov was unveiled on the main administration building of [[I.I. Mechnikov Odessa National University]].<ref>"Chebotaryov, Nikolai Grigorievich." Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography. 2008 - https://www.encyclopedia.com/doc/1G2-2830900875.html</ref>
